social.facebook_caption:
Ever glance at your smartwatch on tirzepatide and wonder, "wait, is that right?"

A faster pulse is actually on the label. The Zepbound (tirzepatide) label lists a heart rate increase under side effects. In two pooled trials in adults with obesity or overweight (one trial without type 2 diabetes, one with it), heart rate rose by 1 to 3 beats per minute on average, compared with no increase on placebo.

Chest pain, fainting or shortness of breath? Call your emergency number right away. A racing heartbeat at rest that doesn't settle? Contact your prescriber or your local urgent care. For anything that isn't one of those emergency signs, don't stop or change your medicine on your own. Talk to your prescriber first.

Save this for your next check-in.

#Tirzepatide #GLP1

Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

factcheck.summary:
I checked the one factual claim against the live Zepbound label on DailyMed (revised 28 Aug 2026). Section 6.1 says: "In a pool of Study 1 and 2, treatment with ZEPBOUND resulted in a mean increase in heart rate of 1 to 3 beats per minute compared to no increase in placebo-treated patients." Slide 2 matches this: same number, same "on average" framing, same comparison with placebo. Study 1 left out people with type 2 diabetes and Study 2 enrolled only people with it, so "with or without type 2 diabetes" is accurate for the pooled data. It just isn't as exact as it could be. The safety content is sound:
- emergency signs (chest pain, fainting, shortness of breath) say to call the emergency number right away
- a racing heartbeat that doesn't settle goes to the prescriber or local urgent care
- the don't-stop line is limited to non-emergency signs
- the disclaimer and prescriber line close the piece, in the right order.

The title delivers what it promises. Both source URLs work. The Lilly PDF loaded but its text couldn't be extracted, so I used DailyMed to confirm the wording and the date. There are no major or critical issues. The three minor fixes below are all copy-pasteable.

issues.claim: In two pooled trials in adults with obesity or overweight, with or without type 2 diabetes…
issues.problem: This is accurate but vague. The label pools one trial that left out type 2 diabetes (Study 1) and one that enrolled only people with it (Study 2). Our scope rules ask for each trial's population to be named exactly.
issues.fix: The Zepbound (tirzepatide) label lists a heart rate increase under side effects. In two pooled trials in adults with obesity or overweight (one without type 2 diabetes, one with it), heart rate rose by 1 to 3 beats per minute on average, compared with no increase on placebo.

issues.problem: The muted-viewer and craft notes ask for a stat card that names the drug, both groups and the measure. The key number is currently only in the body text.
issues.fix: Set stat to: "+1–3 bpm on average (tirzepatide) vs 0 on placebo"

issues.problem: The craft notes ask for the exact live revised date, not just the month.
issues.fix: Set year to "Revised 28 Aug 2026" for both entries.

issues.fix: Delete the line "Have you noticed your resting pulse change since starting?" and its blank line, so "Save this for your next check-in." is followed directly by "#Tirzepatide #GLP1".

issues.problem: The line leaves out the population and the fact that this comes from pooled trials, and "vs placebo" could be read as a difference from placebo rather than "vs no increase on placebo". The safety block already pushes Threads past 300 characters, so this tightened line keeps the meaning without adding much length.
